title: The lights on the eave
venue: the coast community-college paper, Newport · the laundromat digest
source: lore/drift_wood/_THE_COMPLETE_RUN.md (1999–2000 · deepening xix · the daily filled)
logline: The uncle puts a string of lights on the shack's eave. Half of them work. Gully says that's more than last year. Wood draws the dark ones too.

panels.composition: The shack. The UNCLE on a ladder with a string of lights, GULLY feeding it up. Rain. WOOD and BARNABY below.

image.prompt: an old man on a ladder stringing lights along a shingle shack's eave while a teenager feeds the string up, a young man and a dog below in rain, black and white, no words

panels.composition: The plug going in. The string: lit, dark, lit, dark, dark, lit.

image.prompt: close on a string of holiday lights along an eave with half the bulbs dark, black and white, no words
a stocky teenager looking up at a half-lit string of lights, black and white, no words

panels.composition: The shack at dusk with the lights, half of them. Wood drawing every bulb, the dark ones as circles. The strip counts what's out.

image.prompt: a shingle shack at a boat launch at dusk with a half-lit string of lights along the eave, a young man drawing below, black and white, no words

art.line: brush-pen, committed; black and white; xerox

notes: Half the string lit. The dark bulbs drawn as circles. (Dec 21 shows the string.)
